headline: Broad-based growth continues; legal costs cap margin gains
summary_short: Zillow's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 18% y/y to $708M, with net income up 475% y/y to $46M and diluted EPS of $0.19, as Rentals (+42%) and Mortgages (+56%) outgrew Residential (+8%); Adjusted EBITDA of $182M held flat at a 26% margin despite a 160bp legal-cost headwind.
summary_long: Residential revenue grew 8% y/y on Premier Agent/Showcase/New Construction gains; Mortgages jumped 56% as purchase loan origination volume nearly doubled to $1.5B; Rentals rose 42% on 20% more multifamily unique visitors. Cost of revenue rose 36% on Redfin rentals-syndication lead costs and mortgage processing volume. Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 26% (would have been 27% ex. $11M incremental legal costs). Net cash from operations rose 92% to $200M; Adjusted free cash flow rose 44% to $127M. The company repurchased $626M of stock, cutting cash to $678M and equity to $4.41B. Zillow guided Q2 revenue to $750M-$765M and Adjusted EBITDA to $150M-$165M, plus continued ~30% FY Rentals growth.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based growth: Residential +8% (Premier Agent, Showcase, New Construction), Mortgages +56% (loan origination volume +96% to $1.5B), Rentals +42% (multifamily +57%).
Rose 13% y/y, trailing the 18% revenue gain as a 36% rise in cost of revenue (led by Redfin lead-acquisition costs) compressed gross margin.
Shard-basis (Yahoo) EBITDA, not the company's own $182M non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA; not separately explained in the release.
Yahoo's net-income-plus-tax-and-interest proxy; tracks the swing in pre-tax and net income from very small prior-period bases.
GAAP operating income swung to $36M from -$11M (q/q) / -$9M (y/y) as revenue growth outpaced opex; not separately explained in the release.
Rose 475% y/y to $46M (6.5% margin, +520bp) on revenue growth and cost discipline despite $11M of incremental legal expense.
Tracks net income growth, amplified by a lower diluted share count after $626M of buybacks this quarter.
Matched diluted EPS at $0.19 (vs. $0.03 y/y); dilution had negligible incremental impact this quarter.
Rose $50M (36%) y/y on $38M higher lead-acquisition costs (Redfin rentals syndication), $5M more mortgage loan-processing costs, and $3M each of ad-serving and software/hardware costs.
Rose to $48M from $8M y/y, tracking the operating-income swing plus other income, net, partly offset by $4M of interest expense.
Rose 92% y/y to $200M, consistent with the swing to profitability; the release doesn't break out working-capital detail.
Fell to $34M from $36M y/y; not discussed as a discrete driver in the release.

Broad-based revenue growth across all segments drove net income up 475% y/y even as legal costs held Adjusted EBITDA margin flat at 26%; Q2 guidance calls for $750M-$765M revenue and continued ~30% FY Rentals growth.
